title: Acyclic open extensions in an etale compactification
statement: Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, $u:U\to X$ a separated quasi-compact etale morphism of arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-etale-morphism], and $u=pj$ a compactification with $j:U\to Z$ open and $p:Z\to X$ proper. For every constant-$A$ module sheaf $F$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, $j_!F$ is $p_*$-acyclic: $R^qp_*(j_!F)=0$ for every integer $q>0$ [def-sp-acyclic]. The scheme, morphism, and functor notions used here are those of [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-open-immersion].

source.place: Tag 0GKM (lemma-Rf-shriek-for-quasi-finite), finite-direct-image computation, applied locally to geometric fibres; proper base change identifies those fibres. The arbitrary-base proof is implemented by the agent with the existing Lean APIs.

proof.text: Test the positive classical derived image on all geometric inverse images. Identify it with positive homology of Rp_* applied to j_!F in degree zero, using exactness to move the geometric inverse image through homology.

Combine unbounded proper base change for p with inverse open-extension base change. This identifies the resulting object with compact support on the etale geometric fibre applied to the pullback of F in degree zero.

The geometric fibre map v is quasi-compact and etale over a field, hence finite by Mathlib IsFinite.of_locallyQuasiFinite over the Artinian target (Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/QuasiFinite.lean). In particular v is proper. For its compactification c' the open immersion is proper, since its composite with the separated proper projection is v, and therefore has closed range. Its extension by zero agrees with ordinary direct image. This is exactly the source clopen comparison isIso_openImmersionLowerShriekToLowerStar_of_isClosed_range. Transport its exactness across that isomorphism, compose derived direct images using rightDerivedLowerStarComp, and use exactness of finite direct image. Thus the fibre compact-support functor is the degreewise ordinary direct image for the finite map v. This avoids the Noetherian normalization theorem altogether.

Exact inverse image and the exact finite direct image preserve concentration in degree zero. Hence every positive homology group in the fibre is zero. Transfer this vanishing through the preceding explicit isomorphisms and use conservative geometric inverse images to conclude.

theorem etaleCompactification_acyclic
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    {U X : Scheme.{u}} (u : U ⟶ X) [Etale u] [IsSeparated u] [QuasiCompact u]
    (c : Compactification u) (F : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) :
    (lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.g).rightAcyclic
      ((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c.i).obj F)
